test_title: PYST 26: SSC MTS 2024 - General Awareness (Held On: 18 Oct, 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: By which of the following Amendments was the right to property removed from Part III of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**44th Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **44th Amendment Act** of the Indian Constitution, enacted in **1978**, removed the right to property from the category of Fundamental Rights under Part III of the Constitution.
 
• After the amendment, the right to property was reclassified as a **legal right** under Article 300A in Part XII of the Constitution.
 
• This change was made during the tenure of the **Janata Party government**, led by Prime Minister **Morarji Desai**.
 
• The primary objective of this amendment was to facilitate **land reforms** and prevent misuse of the right to property by affluent individuals to challenge government policies.
 
• Post-amendment, property disputes are dealt with as violations of legal rights rather than Fundamental Rights, ensuring streamlined governance and justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights in Part III**

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Articles 12 to 35 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These rights are essential for safeguarding individual freedoms and are enforceable by the courts.
 
• Major Fundamental Rights include the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
 
 
• **Legal Rights vs Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are protected by the Constitution and cannot be altered without constitutional amendment.
 
• Legal rights are granted by ordinary legislation and can be modified or revoked by the legislature.
 
• The 44th Amendment reclassified the right to property as a legal right under Article 300A.
 
 
 
• **Article 300A of the Constitution**
 
 
• Article 300A states: "No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law."
 
• This provision ensures that property can only be taken by the government through legally established procedures.
 
 
 
• **Land Reforms in India**
 
 
• Land reforms aim to redistribute land ownership and increase agricultural productivity.
 
• The removal of the right to property as a Fundamental Right facilitated initiatives like the abolition of the zamindari system and ceilings on landholding.
